newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Mir crew seek leak in damaged cooling system.
newsitem.headline: Mir crew seek leak in damaged cooling system.

text.p: The crew of Russia's orbiting Mir space station are trying to locate a leak in its damaged cooling system, a mission control spokesman said on Monday.
The spokesman said that toxic fumes had recently appeared inside the 11-year-old station but added that the three-man crew were not in danger.
"The level of air contamination in the station is very low but it has managed to cause eye irritation for cosmonaut Alexander Lazutkin," the spokesman told Reuters.
"It is a very complicated task to determine the place of the leak. The crew is working on this task," he said.
U.S. cosmonaut Jerry Linenger said recently he and his two Russian colleagues had twice almost abandoned the station in the past few months because of the leaking coolant.
Temperature and humidity aboard the station soared after the cooling system failed and the crew were forced to take parts from another device to fix Mir's main oxygen generators.
The spokesman said the Mir crew had made medical experiments on Monday and had also taken physical exercises.

"The crew also prepared for a spacewalk which is expected on April 29, with the participation of the U.S. astronaut Jerry Linenger, who has been aboard Mir for almost three months," the spokesman said.
Russia and Western countries are currently preparing for the launch of the Alpha International Space Station, which is expected to replace Mir by 2003.
